title: Archery
statementMd:
Last summer you were watching all the matches in the 2012 Olympics in London. One of the interesting sports is archery (it's the game of propelling arrows with the use of a bow to hit a target), but in this problem we are dealing with a new type of archery.

In this new type of archery, the player has arrows that can penetrate any target and can go to infinity (the same arrow may hit more than one target), and there will be a lot of targets around the player everywhere, and the targets may intersect and/or overlap with each others.

From the top view you can model the targets as line segments and the player as a point at the origin (point (0,0) is the origin), also there will be no target which intersects with the player's position.

You are really interested to calculate the expected number of targets this player can penetrate using one arrow, if he will shoot his arrow in a random direction (there are infinite number of different directions, and each direction has the same probability to be used for the random shoot).

For example, the following figure explains the first sample test, where the player is at the origin, and there are two targets $*T*_{1}$ with end points (1,5) and (3,3), and $*T*_{2}$ with end points (3,5) and (6,2), you can notice that there is a region where the player can shoot an arrow and penetrate the two targets, and there are two regions where he can penetrate only one target, and the last region he will not penetrate any target.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c2b862d41ba66331db073b94c2e3bba4b99a256a.png)

*Note that a target can be hit at any point between its 2 end points (inclusive).*

## Input

The input starts with a line containing one integer ***N*** (1 $≤$ ***N*** $≤$ 100) representing the number of targets in the game. Followed by ***N*** lines, the **i*th*** line contains 4 integers separated by a single space ***$*X*_{1}$*** ***$*Y*_{1}$*** ***$*X*_{2}$*** ***$*Y*_{2}$*** (-100 $≤$ ***$*X*_{1}$***, ***$*Y*_{1}$***, ***$*X*_{2}$***, ***$*Y*_{2}$*** $≤$ 100) representing the **i*th*** target end points (***$*X*_{1}$***,***$*Y*_{1}$***) and (***$*X*_{2}$***,***$*Y*_{2}$***).

## Output

Print on a single line, the expected number of targets the player can penetrate using one arrow. The absolute or relative error in the answer should not exceed $10^{ - 6}$.
statementZhMd:
去年夏天，你观看了 2012 年伦敦奥运会的所有比赛。其中一项有趣的运动是射箭（即用弓射出箭来命中靶子的运动），不过在本题中，我们要研究一种新型射箭运动。

在这种新型射箭运动中，选手的箭能够穿透任何靶子，并一直飞向无穷远处（同一支箭可能命中多个靶子）。选手四周分布着许多靶子，这些靶子可能相交和/或重叠。

从俯视角度看，可以将靶子建模为线段，将选手建模为位于原点的一个点（点 (0,0) 为原点）。没有任何靶子经过选手所在的位置。

你很想计算：如果选手朝一个随机方向射出一支箭，他能穿透的靶子数量的期望是多少（不同的方向有无穷多个，随机射箭时各个方向被选中的概率相同）。

例如，下图展示了第一个样例。选手位于原点，有两个靶子：$*T*_{1}$ 的端点为 (1,5) 和 (3,3)，$*T*_{2}$ 的端点为 (3,5) 和 (6,2)。可以看到，有一个区域内的射击方向能让箭穿透两个靶子，有两个区域内的射击方向只能让箭穿透一个靶子，而在最后一个区域内射击则不会穿透任何靶子。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c2b862d41ba66331db073b94c2e3bba4b99a256a.png)

*注意，箭可以命中靶子两个端点之间的任意一点（包括端点）。*

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含一个整数 ***N***（1 $≤$ ***N*** $≤$ 100），表示游戏中靶子的数量。接下来有 ***N*** 行，第 ***i*** 行包含 4 个用单个空格分隔的整数 ***$*X*_{1}$*** ***$*Y*_{1}$*** ***$*X*_{2}$*** ***$*Y*_{2}$***（-100 $≤$ ***$*X*_{1}$***, ***$*Y*_{1}$***, ***$*X*_{2}$***, ***$*Y*_{2}$*** $≤$ 100），表示第 ***i*** 个靶子的两个端点 (***$*X*_{1}$***,***$*Y*_{1}$***) 和 (***$*X*_{2}$***,***$*Y*_{2}$***)。

## 输出格式

在一行中输出选手用一支箭能够穿透的靶子数量的期望。答案的绝对误差或相对误差不得超过 $10^{ - 6}$。
